headline: High: ctx can write files and observe Claude Code events while Rasa can egress to chat APIs, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events and has filesystem access, so it can ingest content that may later be treated as instructions. Rasa exposes multiple chat channels and network egress, but no direct shared channel is documented. The pairwise bridge is plausible via files or copied outputs, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF ctx reads untrusted file or tool-output content and forwards it into downstream prompts
IF Rasa relays ctx-generated text into a channel that operators or automations treat as instructions
mitigations: Restrict ctx to trusted directories only
Add provenance tags to ctx outputs
Disable automatic ingestion of Rasa transcripts into ctx
Review any copied text before reuse
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, harness records, and filesystem content; Rasa handles text/voice and can egress to allowlisted APIs. No shared workspace is documented, but if operators bridge them through files or transcripts, sensitive ctx data can flow into Rasa outputs or external channels. The interaction is indirect, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF ctx outputs logs or graph data into a file that Rasa ingests
IF Rasa sends conversation content derived from ctx artifacts to an external API
mitigations: Keep ctx artifacts in a separate directory
Redact logs before handoff to Rasa
Limit Rasa channels to non-sensitive test data
Turn off transcript forwarding where possible
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and writes to filesystem-related surfaces, while Rasa does not support multiple instances and has allowlisted network egress. There is no documented shared mutable resource or lockless concurrent write path between them, so direct conflict is limited. The main risk is operational overlap rather than destructive contention.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an operator runs concurrent jobs that mutate the same external resource
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Serialize any shared-resource updates
Document ownership of mutable resources
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is designed to observe tool events and manage context, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative summaries. Rasa is a dialogue system that can turn text into user-facing responses or actions, making a misread handoff plausible. Because no verification boundary is documented, errors can cascade from ctx into Rasa-generated replies or workflows.
conditions: IF Rasa uses ctx summaries as source material without validation
IF ctx emits incorrect facts that Rasa repeats to end users
mitigations: Require human review of ctx summaries
Add a verification step before Rasa responses
Mark ctx output as untrusted metadata
Sample-check downstream replies for factual drift
requires-engineering: implement citation/traceability checks

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, which can carry retention or residency obligations, while Rasa handles text and voice and routes through messaging APIs. No specific jurisdictional mismatch is documented for either agent, so this is a compliance-overlap concern rather than a proven breach. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from cross-system data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ctx logs and then forwarded through Rasa channels
IF retention policies differ between ctx artifacts and Rasa transcripts
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Set short retention on transcripts and logs
Separate test and production conversations
Review data-handling settings in both systems
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
